recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not reapply the original FHIR-6118 409-on-If-Match-failure wording; future changes to contention status-code policy should be handled by a new FHIR-I HTTP decision that accounts for FHIR-16096.
issue_request: FHIR-6118 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core HTTP change request from DSTU1. It questioned update/version conflict handling that used 409 when update ignores meta.versionId, asked that the rejecting-updates status-code list point down to Managing Resource Contention, and recorded the then-approved rule that 409 was the actual conflict status while 412 applied when a server required contention-management preconditions such as ETag/If-Match headers.
initial_application: The Jira comments cite svn revision 5962. Git commit d26d81284b80a97dd876119b88e0f14846d25fb1 is that revision and changed source/http.html to link the 409/412 error-list entry to #concurrency and to use 409 Conflict for a non-matching If-Match while keeping 412 Pre-condition failed for a missing required If-Match.
additional_context: The current combined branch source/http.html is the active RESTful API page linked from the Exchange module. Its error-list entry still links 409 Conflict/412 Precondition Failed version conflict management to #concurrency below. The old status-code mapping should not be restored because later Published/Persuasive FHIR-16096 corrected the HTTP semantics to 412 for failed If-Match preconditions, 400 Bad Request for a missing server-required If-Match, and 409 Conflict for other server-detected conflicts such as pessimistic locking. FHIR-16096 is already represented on the combined branch by audit commit a07984311cda53cd6da7401cb4ce412dfa5fbbb9. Later FHIR-31927 was Resolved - No Change and did not add alternate contention mechanisms.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already carries the still-valid FHIR-6118 cross-reference, and its different status-code mapping is intentional later policy from FHIR-16096 rather than a missed FHIR-6118 application.
